results.content: With highly contested midterm elections in a few weeks, President Donald Trump again sees his approval rating stuck at a career-low in Reuters/Ipsos polling, which also indicated cratering support from Hispanic voters. The new poll, released on Monday, Oct. 5, found that only 32% of Americans approved of the president’s job performance. Trump’s current approval rating, which has now sat at 32% in two consecutive polls, is the lowest he has seen in Reuters/Ipsos polling during both terms in office. results.content: Likely voters prefer Democratic candidates over Republican candidates by 16 points in the November congressional elections, their largest lead in any Economist / YouGov Poll this year so far. This 16-point Democratic lead among likely voters is far larger than their 6-point lead among currently registered voters, or the 9-point Democratic lead among voters who are either registered to vote or say they will register by Election Day.
